newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen end down but off lows on rate report.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen end down but off lows on rate report.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures finished easier but off their lows on Friday following a news report which triggered afternoon sales on concerns about Japanese interest rates.

A Jiji news report quoted a senior Bank of Japan (BOJ) official as saying the central bank was concerned about an excessive decline in long-term interest rates. The BOJ declined to comment on the report.

March Euroyen fell to a low of 99.15 on the back of the report, but recovered to close at 99.19 against its CME close at 99.21. December JGBs, which were more sharply sold off, settled at 121.63 against their opening 121.84.

"The Jiji story was the big one. But the move was made bigger by all the weary longs in the market. The technicals had been calling for a correction," said a trader at a European institution. "But all the volatility was in the long end."
He said talk of Japan's industrial production data, due on Monday, being lower than expected had bolstered optimism that Japanese interest rates would remain low until year end.
Eurodollar futures ended slightly lower after hovering in a three-tick range, with the most active December contract at 94.25 against its IMM settlement at 94.24.
